name: Using Ingested Poisons

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Using Ingested Poisons
You use an action to sprinkle poison onto food or drink.
A creature that consumes the substance is exposed to
the poison. If you might be observed, you must make an
Agility attack roll and compare the total of the roll to the
Perception scores of anyone that can see you. A success
means they didn’t notice you administer the poison,
while a failure means they did. The GM might grant
boons or impose banes based on the situation.
Some ingested poisons must be inhaled. You use an
action to blow the poison into a target creature’s face.
The target must succeed on an Agility challenge roll or
be exposed to the poison.

name: Using Injected Poisons

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Using Injected Poisons
You can use an injected poison by loading it into a
syringe or needle ring (see those entries below) or by
using an action to apply the poison to the edge or point
of a weapon or piece of ammunition. The poisonous
weapon or ammunition retains its potency for 1 hour or
until it deals damage, whichever occurs ﬁrst.

name: Using Harvested Venom

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Using Harvested Venom
Harvested venom can be used only as an injected poison.
It functions as described in the creature’s statistics. If
harvested from a dead specimen, challenge rolls to resist
the poison are made with 1 boon.

name: Creating Poisons

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Creating Poisons
Characters with suitable professions can brew poisons
using the rules for creating equipment described in
Demon Lord’s Companion. However, the needed raw
materials have the same availability as the poisons
they would create. For example, creating lethal poison
requires access to exotic ingredients. Characters might
have to travel to a large city or explore a potentially
dangerous area to ﬁnd the substances needed, as
the GM decides.
Assassins (Shadow, page 62) have the Manufacture
Poison talent and poisoners (Shadow, page 93) have the
Poison Mastery talent. Both talents permit characters to
rapidly create the typical poison described in chapter 6
of the main rulebook.
